--- title: "GLORYS Identical-Twin Chain" jupyter: python3 fig-dpi: 300 bibliography: ../paper/references.bib --- ```{=html} ``` This report runs the identical-twin chain of the theory note (`paper/sections/theory.tex`, validation design) on boxes A, B and A $\cup$ B for 2015--2019. GLORYS12 velocity $u$ and OHC $Z$ are fixed. The randomness is the deployments, drawn from the year-stratified smoothed bootstrap $\mathcal D_c$ of the real 2010--2019 launches. Each replicate is one array advected at park depth in GLORYS. # Estimand and estimators For box $A$ and year $y$, $\mathcal X_y=A^{\mathrm{deep}}\times\mathcal T_y$, with $\mathbb P_y=\mu(\cdot\cap\mathcal X_y)/\mu(\mathcal X_y)$, $\mu=\alpha\otimes\mathrm{Leb}$, and $\theta_y=\int Z\,d\mathbb P_y$. $Z$ is constant on native $1/12^\circ$ cell-days, so $\theta_y$ is an exact finite sum. Per replicate and box-year: * **naive**: the mean of $Z$ at the in-box profiles; * **Hájek**: $\sum_i v_iZ_i/\sum_i v_i$, $v_i=1/\hat q_{-r}(x_i)$; * **map** $\hat\theta_{\mathrm K}=Q_y(\hat m)$: the local mean field [@sukianto2026, eq. 5] plus local simple kriging of its anomaly [@kuusela2018], with covariance plug-ins fit once to the GLORYS anomaly lattice (so external to every replicate). $Q_y$ is the $0.5^\circ\times$ three-nodes-per-month quadrature, and the year is the day-weighted mean of its months; **mean field** is $Q_y(\hat\mu)$ alone. The map data also include the 265 floats alive at the 2010-01-01 start of the record. They are fixed by design (not drawn from $\mathcal D_c$), so they are never held out and never $1/\hat q$-weighted; * **DR**: $\hat\theta_{\mathrm{DR}}=K^{-1}\sum_k\{Q_y(\hat m_{-k})+\hat C_k\}$, $K=5$, with $\hat C_k$ the Hájek mean of the held-out residuals $e_k=Z-\hat m_{-k}$ at fold-$k$ profiles, weighted by $1/\hat q_k$, $\hat q_k=\sum_cn_{k,c}\hat q^{(1)}_{c,-r}$. Folds are a random permutation of floats within cohort (launch year), so $n_{k,c}\in\{\lfloor N_c/K\rfloor, \lceil N_c/K\rceil\}$. The fold maps are exact leave-fold-out refits by Gram and block downdates of the full fit. One convention departs from exact: which mean-field centres get fitted (at least 60 profiles) and the ridge scale ($10^{-8}\operatorname{tr}G$) are taken from the full data. A direct refit without one fold changes the fold-map box means by under $10^{-5}$ GJ m$^{-2}$. **Intensity.** $\hat q^{(1)}_c$ is the edge-corrected Gaussian kernel estimate ($\sigma_s=1/6^\circ$, $\sigma_t=2$ d; see the bandwidth sensitivity below), evaluated exactly at the points (unbinned). $\hat q^{(1)}_{c,-r}$ drops replicate $r$'s own profiles. The kernel is a sum over replicates, so this is exact: $\hat q^{(1)}_{c,-r}=(RN_c\hat q^{(1)}_c-\kappa_{c,r})/((R-1)N_c)$, with $\kappa_{c,r}$ the (edge-corrected) kernel sum over replicate $r$'s cohort-$c$ profiles. It makes $1/\hat q$ independent of the weighted array, which Campbell's theorem requires. **Variance.** $\hat{\mathcal V}_k$ is the float-cluster estimator of the theory note (Prop. var., part 3): per-float totals of $v_i(e_k-\hat C_k)$, centred within cohort, including the fold-$k$ floats that never reach $\mathcal X_y$. The interval is $\hat\theta_{\mathrm{DR}}\pm1.96(K^{-2}\sum_k\hat{\mathcal V}_k)^{1/2}$, a heuristic that ignores between-fold covariance. # (1) Preferential sampling: naive bias and $\operatorname{Cov}(\hat w,Z)$ For the naive mean, $\mathbb E\sum_iZ_i/\mathbb E n=\int Zq\,d\mathbb P_y/\int q\,d\mathbb P_y=\theta_y+\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathbb P_y}(w,Z)$ exactly, with $w=q/\bar q_y$. The naive estimator's own bias differs from this by the ratio remainder, which is $O(1/n)$. The table reports three quantities: * the Monte Carlo mean of naive $-\,\theta_y$ over all replicates; * the pooled ratio $\sum_r\sum_iZ_i/\sum_rn_r-\theta_y$, which *equals* $\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathbb P_y}(\tilde w,Z)$ for the pooled native-cell occupancy $\tilde w$; * $\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathbb P_y}(\hat w,Z)$ with $\hat w=\hat q/\bar{\hat q}_y$ from the binned native-grid kernel ($\sigma_s=1/6^\circ$, $\sigma_t=4$ d). Its gap to the previous column is kernel smoothing error. ::: {#tbl-align .cell tbl-cap='Naive bias and alignment of the sampling intensity with OHC (GJ per m2), all replicates; qmin_rel is the minimum over the box-year of q-hat relative to its mean.' execution_count=3}

::: ::: **Quadrature remainder.** The map estimates $Q_y(\hat m)$, so its error is $Q_y(\hat m)-\theta_y=Q_y(\hat m-Z)+\{Q_y(Z)-\theta_y\}$. The second term, the quadrature remainder, is what a perfect map would still miss. The table below evaluates it from the true $Z$ at the node-times against the native-cell $\theta_y$. $Z$ is piecewise constant on native cells, and each node, the area centroid of a $0.5^\circ$ cell's $6\times6$ native block, sits on a native cell corner. So $Z$ at a node is taken as the mean of the four cells meeting there. A containing-cell lookup breaks the tie to one side, a $1/24^\circ$ shift that reads $+0.12$ GJ m$^{-2}$ too warm across the box B front. The remainder is below 0.01 GJ m$^{-2}$ everywhere, so the map errors above are interpolation error. ::: {#tbl-quad .cell tbl-cap='Quadrature remainder Q_y(Z) - theta_y of the map functional applied to the true field (GJ per m2).' execution_count=5}

Top: naive profile mean.](glorys_chain_files/figure-html/errors-output-2.png){#errors-1 width=1199 height=713} ## Box B ![](glorys_chain_files/figure-html/errors-output-4.png){#errors-2 width=1199 height=713} ## Box A u B ![](glorys_chain_files/figure-html/errors-output-6.png){#errors-3 width=1199 height=713} ::: ::: # How the DR correction reweights the kriging residuals Fold $k$'s correction targets $T_k=\theta_y-Q_y(\hat m_{-k})$, the area mean of the map error field $Z-\hat m_{-k}$, using the held-out residuals $e_k(x_i)$ at fold-$k$ profiles. Floats crowd where $q$ is large, so the unweighted residual mean estimates $\int e_k\,q\,d\mathbb P_y/\int q\,d\mathbb P_y$ instead of $T_k$. The weights $1/\hat q_k$ undo that tilt (Campbell's theorem). @fig-intensity shows the tilt itself. @fig-dr-example takes one replicate-year (box B 2017, replicate 171, picked for its large map error: map $+0.45$, DR $-0.02$ GJ m$^{-2}$). @fig-corrections shows the effect over all replicates. ::: {#cell-fig-intensity .cell execution_count=9} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Box A (south) and box B (north), 2017. Right: per fold, the target T_k, the unweighted residual mean and the 1/q-hat-weighted correction C_k (GJ per m2).](glorys_chain_files/figure-html/fig-dr-example-output-1.png){#fig-dr-example width=1182 height=454} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-corrections .cell execution_count=11} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![All 200 replicates, years and folds: unweighted residual mean (grey) and the correction C_k (blue) against the target T_k; the line is 1:1, and the means of each minus T_k are printed.](glorys_chain_files/figure-html/fig-corrections-output-1.png){#fig-corrections width=1309 height=451} ::: ::: Single folds are noisy. In the example, two of five folds correct in the wrong direction, and DR relies on the average over folds: $K^{-1}\sum_k\hat C_k=-0.53$ against $K^{-1}\sum_kT_k=-0.51$. Over all replicates the unweighted residual mean misses $T_k$ by $-0.21$ GJ m$^{-2}$ in box B and $-0.05$ in box A, the residual analogue of the naive bias. Weighting by $1/\hat q_k$ cuts this to $-0.04$ and $-0.015$. The rest is the kernel smoothing bias of the bandwidth sensitivity below. **MSE decomposition (Prop. mse).** Per fold, the error is $\hat\theta_k-\theta_y=\hat C_k-T_k=\beta_k+\xi_k$, with $T_k=\theta_y-Q_y(\hat m_{-k})$. So $\mathbb E(\hat C_k-T_k)^2=\mathbb E\beta_k^2+\mathbb E\mathcal V_k$, and $\mathbb E\hat{\mathcal V}_k$ estimates the second term. DR gains on the map when $\mathbb ET^2$ exceeds $\mathbb E(\hat C_k-T_k)^2$ (Eq. mse-sufficient, fold by fold). `cover_min` is the smallest $\min_{\mathcal X_y}\hat q_k/\bar{\hat q}_k$ over replicates and folds, the Ass. cover check at the map nodes. ::: {#tbl-mse .cell tbl-cap='Fold-level MSE terms (GJ2 per m4): E T^2, E (C - T)^2, mean V-hat, mean of C - T (GJ per m2), minimum coverage ratio, mean fold ESS.' execution_count=12}

::: # Multi-year targets The same replicate's annual estimates give any linear functional of $(\theta_y)_y$, here the year-to-year changes $\theta_{y+1}-\theta_y$, the 2015--2019 change and the day-weighted five-year mean. Bias is the same functional of the annual biases. Variance also needs the between-year covariance of the errors within a replicate, which is small for both estimators (mean correlation about 0.1 for the map, 0--0.04 for DR): changes add the annual variances while a persistent bias cancels, and the five-year mean divides the variance by about five while the bias remains. ::: {#tbl-derived .cell tbl-cap='Map and DR error for year-to-year changes, the 2015-2019 change and the five-year mean (GJ per m2); dMSE is map minus DR (GJ2 per m4).' execution_count=13} ::: {.panel-tabset} ## Box A

::: ::: # Kernel bandwidth sensitivity The weights enter DR through $\beta^{\mathrm{prod}}\approx\int e_k(q/\hat q_k-1)\,d\mathbb P_y$, so a kernel error aligned with the map residual biases the correction. The fold maps and residuals are fixed; only $\hat q$ is rebuilt, on the $3\times3$ grid $\sigma_s\in\{1/12^\circ,1/6^\circ,1/3^\circ\}$, $\sigma_t\in\{2,4,8\}$ d, for the same 200 replicates. The DR bias moves monotonically toward zero as either bandwidth narrows (box B: $-0.10$ at $(1/3^\circ,8\text{ d})$, $-0.02$ at $(1/12^\circ,2\text{ d})$), which identifies it as kernel smoothing bias. Narrower kernels raise the variance and drive $\min\hat q_k/\bar{\hat q}_k$ toward zero (Ass. cover), so production uses $(1/6^\circ,2\text{ d})$, the smallest box B RMSE on the grid. The variance ratio $\operatorname{Var}/\mathbb E\hat{\mathcal V}$ does not depend on the bandwidth.
